age.short_description: Age group; "Total" is the all-ages aggregate.
age.long_description: Age group as reported by ABCs. "Total" is the all-ages aggregate and overlaps the specific bands, so exclude it when summing across ages. The bands differ by file because CDC reports different stratifications per pathogen and topic: the pneumococcal serotype data uses <5 years / 5-49 years / 50+ years; strep case and death rates use <1 / 1 / 2-4 / 5-17 / 18-34 / 35-49 / 50-64 / 65+; and the strep resistance and typing files use the coarser <1 / 18-64 / 65+. ABCs reports no 2-17 band for Group B, and its 18-64 / 65+ split does not line up with the 18-49 / 50-64 bands used elsewhere in this repo - both are source-determined. The aggregate level is "Total", matching the label used across the rest of the database (it outnumbers "Overall" 40 to 3 in bundle outputs).

N_SSUAD.short_name: Number of non-invasive pneumococcal pneumonia episodes
N_SSUAD.long_name: Number of non-invasive pneumococcal pneumonia episodes

pct_IPD.long_name: Percent of IPD episodes caused by the indicated serotype

spn_surveillance_population.short_description: Total population under active surveillance for invasive pneumococcal disease in the ABCs catchment area
spn_surveillance_population.long_description: The number of persons living within the ABCs catchment area for pneumococcal disease surveillance in a given year. Catchment areas vary by state and over time as surveillance regions have expanded. The national total reflects the sum across the 8 sites that consistently report to ABCs (CA, CT, GA, MD, MN, NY, OR, TN).
spn_surveillance_population.statement: In {location}, the ABCs surveillance population was {value}.

rate_IPD.long_name: Invasive pneumococcal disease incidence rate per 100,000 population
rate_IPD.short_description: Annual rate of invasive pneumococcal disease cases per 100,000 persons in the ABCs catchment area
rate_IPD.long_description: Incidence rate of invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) per 100,000 population, calculated as the number of IPD cases divided by the ABCs surveillance population multiplied by 100,000. Rates are reported by serotype and age group within the ABCs catchment area.
rate_IPD.statement: In {location}, the IPD incidence rate was {value} per 100,000 population.

sex.long_description: Sex as reported by ABCs. "Total" combines both sexes and must not be summed with the Male and Female rows. Reported for Group A only; Group B rows carry "Overall". The aggregate level is "Total", matching the label used across the rest of the database (it outnumbers "Overall" 40 to 3 in bundle outputs).

race_ethnicity.long_description: Race and ethnicity as reported by ABCs, collapsed to White, Black, and Other. "Total" combines all groups and must not be summed with the specific levels. The aggregate level is "Total", matching the label used across the rest of the database (it outnumbers "Overall" 40 to 3 in bundle outputs).

onset.short_description: Early-onset (0-6 days of life) vs late-onset (7-89 days) infant Group B disease; "Total" is not onset-specific.
onset.long_description: Group B Streptococcus is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis, and CDC splits infant disease by onset timing: early-onset (0-6 days of life, usually acquired around delivery) and late-onset (7-89 days). Rows with "Total" are not onset-specific, so do not sum across this column - the onset rows are a subset of infants, not additional population. CDC's source labels conflate this with age (for example "Infants, early-onset disease"), which the ingest decomposes into age plus onset. The aggregate level is "Total", matching the label used across the rest of the database (it outnumbers "Overall" 40 to 3 in bundle outputs). For case counts a derived "Total" row per age group sums early- and late-onset; for rates no such total is derived, because the onset rates use a different denominator than the age-band rates.

pathogen.short_description: Group A or Group B Streptococcus.
pathogen.long_description: Which organism the row describes: "Group A Streptococcus" (Streptococcus pyogenes) or "Group B Streptococcus" (Streptococcus agalactiae). These are different diseases with different at-risk populations - Group A causes strep throat and invasive disease across all ages, Group B is primarily neonatal sepsis and invasive disease in older adults - so do not pool them. The pneumococcal data in this source (Streptococcus pneumoniae) is a third organism and lives in separate files without this column.

pop.long_name: Population denominator for the ABCs catchment
pop.short_description: Census population for the geography, year, and age group.
pop.long_description: Census-derived population used as the denominator for rate_IPD. Active Bacterial Core surveillance (ABCs) is population-based but covers a defined catchment of selected US counties - roughly 35 million people - not the entire country. Rates are observed within that catchment; counts labelled national are CDC's population-weighted extrapolations. Values are national only, with no state or county breakdown.

Denominator is the isolates tested (abcs_n_isolates). In CDC's current release every value carrying units of "Percent" is stored as a proportion between 0 and 1; the ingest scales these to percentages. Active Bacterial Core surveillance (ABCs) is population-based but covers a defined catchment of selected US counties - roughly 35 million people - not the entire country. Rates are observed within that catchment; counts labelled national are CDC's population-weighted extrapolations. Values are national only, with no state or county breakdown. Gaps are filled with 0 and marked by the matching abcs_not_reported_flag_* column. A flagged 0 is NOT a measured zero - CDC published nothing for that cell - so check the flag before aggregating.

abcs_not_reported_flag_n_isolates.short_description: 1 where CDC did not report abcs_n_isolates for that row and the value was filled with 0; 0 where the value is as published.

Every measure in this source has its own flag, including measures CDC always reports (whose flag is all zeros), so a consumer never has to work out whether a flag exists for the column it cares about - and a shared flag could not distinguish a genuine zero from an unreported one where both occur on the same row. Reasons a cell goes unreported are structural: an antibiotic off that pathogen's susceptibility panel, an emm type or serotype CDC pooled into "other" that year, a rate not broken out for that stratification. Reading a flagged 0 as a measured zero understates resistance, syndrome rates and type shares, so filter on this column before aggregating.

abcs_not_reported_flag_drug_panel.long_name: Flag for values not reported by the source (drug_panel)
abcs_not_reported_flag_drug_panel.short_description: 1 where the source did not report the covered measure(s), 0 otherwise.
abcs_not_reported_flag_drug_panel.long_description: 1 where CDC did not report the measure(s) this flag covers, 0 otherwise. Tetracycline and linezolid are on the Group A susceptibility panel but not the Group B panel, and linezolid was only added to the Group A panel partway through the series. These are genuinely absent rather than suppressed, so the value is left missing rather than imputed - do not read a flagged row as a zero.

rate_denominator.long_name: What the per-100,000 rate is relative to
rate_denominator.short_description: Whether the rate is per 100,000 of the row's own stratum or of the whole population.
rate_denominator.long_description: CDC labels every ABCs rate "Per 100,000 population" while using two different bases, so this column records which applies. "Stratum population" means per 100,000 of the group the row describes - the "<1" age band rate is per 100,000 infants, reading 115.7 for 1997 Group B, consistent with 3,900 infant cases over ~3.9M births. "Population" means per 100,000 of the whole population regardless of the row's stratum, which is how CDC reports the infant early- and late-onset rates - 0.70 + 0.40 = 1.10 for the same year and cases, over ~272M people. The two differ in all 28 years, mean absolute difference 66.3, so rows with different denominators must never be summed or plotted on one axis. "Total" appears where the row is not a rate and the column does not apply.

abcs.name: Active Bacterial Core surveillance (ABCs)
abcs.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
abcs.location: Serotype Data for Invasive Pneumococcal Disease Cases by Age Group from Active Bacterial Core surveillance
abcs.description: CDC monitors invasive bacterial infections that cause bloodstream infections, sepsis, and meningitis in persons living in the community through Active Bacterial Core surveillance (ABCs). ABCs conducts laboratory- and population-based surveillance for invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD). ABCs serotype data are used to measure the impact of vaccine use in the United States on vaccine-type IPD. This table reports IPD case counts in the ABCs catchment area by serotype for years 1998 through 2022. Cases are grouped into the following mutually exclusive age groups: age <2 years old, age 2-4 years old, age 5-17 years old, age 18-49 years old, age 50-64 years old, and age >=65 years old. ABCs methods and surveillance areas reporting IPD cases has changed over time. Given these changes, trends in serotype distribution by year and age group should be interpreted with caution. The all-site summary presented here is calculated based on the 8 sites that consistently report to ABCs and differs from the All-site measure provided by the source. Additional information on ABCs methods and surveillance population is available at https://www.cdc.gov/abcs/methodology/index.html. Analyze and visualize data using the ABCs Bact Facts Interactive Data Dashboard at https://www.cdc.gov/abcs/bact-facts-interactive-dashboard. ABCs IPD Isolates were serotyped by Quellung, PCR, or whole genome sequencing (WGS). Cases without an isolate available or with mixed serotypes reported are listed on the table as MISS. Additionally, non-typeable IPD cases are shown as NT. Zero cell rows were not included in this dataset. Minor changes to previous years serotype data can occur as additional isolates and serotype data become available. Cases were excluded from this dataset if the ABCs site did not perform surveillance in the catchment area for a full calendar year. As a result, cases were excluded from the following sites: TN, 11 counties, Jul-Dec 1999; CO, 5 counties, Jul-Dec 2000; CA, 2 counties (aged <5 years), Oct-Dec 2000.

ssuad.name: Serotype-Specific Urinary Antigen Detection (SSUAD) Study
ssuad.description: The CAAP (Community-Acquired Acute Pneumonia) study by Ramirez et al. (2025) used serotype-specific urinary antigen detection (SSUAD) to identify pneumococcal serotypes causing non-invasive pneumonia in Louisville, Kentucky. This methodology allows identification of pneumococcal serotypes in patients with pneumonia who do not have positive blood cultures, providing insight into the full spectrum of pneumococcal disease burden. The study demonstrates that serotypes causing invasive disease also commonly cause non-invasive pneumonia, validating the use of IPD surveillance data for understanding overall pneumococcal disease patterns.
ssuad.restrictions: Attribution required. Cite Ramirez et al. Open Forum for Infectious Diseases. 2025.

abcs_gas.name: Active Bacterial Core surveillance (ABCs) Group A Streptococcus
abcs_gas.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
abcs_gas.description: Active Bacterial Core surveillance (ABCs) is a collaboration between CDC, state health departments, and universities conducting active, population-based, laboratory-confirmed surveillance for invasive bacterial disease since 1997. CDC publishes a separate dataset per pathogen; this is the Group A Streptococcus one. Active Bacterial Core surveillance (ABCs) is population-based but covers a defined catchment of selected US counties - roughly 35 million people - not the entire country. Rates are observed within that catchment; counts labelled national are CDC's population-weighted extrapolations. Values are national only, with no state or county breakdown. In CDC's current release every value carrying units of "Percent" is stored as a proportion between 0 and 1; the ingest scales these to percentages. Note that CDC restructured this release in 2026: Group A emm types moved from a single topic to one topic per type with the isolate count in the viewby field, and Group A syndromes changed from a percent of cases (1997 on) to a rate per 100,000 (2001 on).
abcs_gas.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.
